input.question: Why is coconut oil considered healthy, even though it is so dense with saturated fat?
input.ground_truth: The saturated fats in coconut oil are in the form of “Medium-chain triglyceride (MCT)” - this basically means your body burns the saturated fats found in coconut oil in the same way it burns carbs. Carbs (and the sat. fats in coconut oil) are used directly for energy rather than being stored as fat in your body. However, just like carbs, if you eat more than your body is able to burn then the excess will indeed be stored as fat.

Now, grown-ups used to think that too many hard blocks (saturated fats) were not good for you, like eating too much candy. But with coconut oil, even though it has lots of these hard blocks, it also has some special blocks that are good for you! These special blocks help your body work well and even help you feel full after eating.

Also, coconut oil is different from other oils with hard blocks. When people studied it, they found out that, for most people, using a little coconut oil doesn’t make them sick or give them too much “yucky stuff” in their blood.

So, even though coconut oil looks like it’s all hard blocks inside, it still can be a good helper for your body—when you use it in small amounts!
